papers.title: Incremental Nonlinear System Identification and Adaptive Particle Filtering Using Gaussian Process
papers.abstract: An incremental/online state dynamic learning method is proposed for identification of the nonlinear Gaussian state space models. The method embeds the stochastic variational sparse Gaussian process as the probabilistic state dynamic model inside a particle filter framework. Model updating is done at measurement sample rate using stochastic gradient descent based optimization implemented in the state estimation filtering loop. The performance of the proposed method is compared with state-of-the-art Gaussian process based batch learning methods. Finally, it is shown that the state estimation performance significantly improves due to the online learning of state dynamics.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该方法用于非线性系统辨识和状态估计，与有限元代理模型或生物力学优化无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address expensive simulation sampling, surrogate modeling, or any aspect of implant or biomechanics design.

summary_zh.method: 在粒子滤波框架内嵌入稀疏高斯过程，并使用随机梯度下降在线更新。
summary_zh.result: 在线学习方法显著提升了状态估计性能。
summary_zh.validation: 与批处理高斯过程方法在数值基准上比较。

summary_en.motivation: To enable online learning of state dynamics in nonlinear Gaussian state space models for improved state estimation.
summary_en.method: Embed a stochastic variational sparse Gaussian process as the probabilistic state dynamic model inside a particle filter and update it via stochastic gradient descent at each measurement.
summary_en.result: The proposed incremental method significantly improves state estimation performance compared to batch Gaussian process methods.
summary_en.validation: Numerical benchmarks against state-of-the-art batch Gaussian process learning methods.

papers.title: Laser-based in situ embedding of metal nanoparticles into bioextruded alginate hydrogel tubes enhances human endothelial cell adhesion
papers.abstract: Alginate is a widely used hydrogel in tissue engineering owing to its simple and non-cytotoxic gelation process, ease of use, and abundance. However, unlike hydrogels derived from mammalian sources such as collagen, alginate does not contain cell adhesion ligands. Here, we present a novel laser ablation technique for the in situ embedding of gold and iron nanoparticles into hydrogels. We hypothesized that integration of metal nanoparticles in alginate could serve as an alternative material because of its chemical biofunctionalization ability (coupling of RGD ligands) to favor cell adhesion. Cytocompatibility and biofunctionality of the gels were assessed by cell culture experiments using fibroblasts and endothelial cells. Nanoparticles with an average particle size of 3 nm (gold) and 6 nm (iron) were generated and stably maintained in alginate for up to 6 months. Using an extrusion system, several centimeter-long alginate tubes with an outer diameter of approximately 3 mm and a wall thickness of approximately 150 μm were manufactured. Confocal microscopy revealed homogeneously distributed nanoparticle agglomerates over the entire tube volume. Endothelial cells seeded on iron-loaded gels showed significantly higher viability and an increased degree of spreading, and the number of attached cells was also elevated in comparison to the control and gold-loaded alginates. We conclude that laser-based in situ integration of iron nanoparticles (⩽0.01 wt.%) in alginate is a straightforward method to generate composite materials that favor the adhesion of endothelial cells. In addition, we show that nanoparticle integration does not impair the alginate’s gelation and 3D biofabrication properties.

summary_zh.motivation: 利用激光嵌入金属纳米颗粒增强藻酸盐水凝胶的细胞粘附性。
summary_zh.method: 采用激光烧蚀技术将金/铁纳米颗粒原位嵌入挤出成型的藻酸盐水凝胶管中。
summary_zh.result: 铁纳米颗粒显著提高内皮细胞的存活率、铺展和粘附数量。
summary_zh.validation: 通过体外细胞培养实验验证细胞相容性和功能性。

summary_en.motivation: To enhance the cell adhesion properties of alginate hydrogels by embedding metal nanoparticles using a laser-based in situ technique.
summary_en.method: Gold and iron nanoparticles were generated by laser ablation and embedded into bioextruded alginate tubes during fabrication.
summary_en.result: Iron nanoparticles (≤0.01 wt.%) improved endothelial cell viability, spreading, and attachment compared to controls.
summary_en.validation: In vitro cell culture assays with fibroblasts and endothelial cells were conducted to assess cytocompatibility and biofunctionality.
